title: Australian Border Force Recruitment 2026: BFORT Guide
metaDescription: Australian Border Force recruitment 2026: BFORT eligibility, 12-month training, recruit pay and selection stages explained for new applicants.
headline: Australian Border Force Recruitment 2026: Eligibility, BFORT Training and Pay

sections.title: Who can join the Australian Border Force?
sections.content:
To apply for the Border Force Officer Recruit Training (BFORT) program you must be an Australian citizen aged 18 or older, and hold at least a Year 10 certificate, a Certificate IV or diploma, a trade certificate, or relevant work experience. You must also be able to obtain an Australian Government security clearance and an Employment Suitability Clearance, and meet the medical and fitness standards for operational work.

The ABF looks for people who act with honesty and integrity, communicate respectfully, work well in teams, and think critically when applying rules to real situations. Presentation matters too: officers are expected to maintain professional dress, grooming and conduct, because they represent Australia's border at airports, seaports and remote posts across the country.

sections.title: What the BFORT program involves
sections.content:
BFORT is a 12-month program that mixes classroom study with on-the-job placements, and recruits are paid from day one at the APS3 classification, currently A$66,839 to A$76,792 plus 15.4 per cent superannuation, with shift penalties and allowances during operational placements. Training covers immigration law, customs and biosecurity procedures, search and detection techniques, and operational safety, and successful graduates move into permanent employment as Border Force Officers.

After graduating you could be posted almost anywhere in Australia, from major city airports to remote locations, and you may be deployed at short notice as operational needs change. The ABF also offers a separate graduate pathway for degree holders: a 10-month intensive program with rotations through different work areas, for applicants with a bachelor degree from an Australian university.

sections.title: The selection process and how to prepare
sections.content:
The BFORT selection process is competitive and multi-staged. Applicants are strongly encouraged to complete the employment suitability self-assessment before applying, and shortlisted candidates typically face psychometric assessment, interviews, medical and fitness checks, and security vetting. The process can take months, so applying early and keeping your documents ready is wise.

To stand out, prepare examples of teamwork, integrity and decision-making under pressure, and research the ABF's role in protecting Australia's border, including its work on immigration compliance, trade enforcement and biosecurity. Strong written communication helps too, since officers produce reports and records that may be used in legal proceedings, and a current driver's licence is expected or must be obtained.

faqs.q: What is the BFORT program in the Australian Border Force?
faqs.a: BFORT stands for Border Force Officer Recruit Training, the Australian Border Force's 12-month entry program for new officers. It combines classroom study with operational placements, covering immigration law, customs procedures, biosecurity, search techniques and officer safety. Recruits are paid at the APS3 level from day one, and successful graduates move into permanent employment as Border Force Officers.

faqs.q: What qualifications do you need to join the Australian Border Force?
faqs.a: You must be an Australian citizen aged 18 or older, and hold at least a Year 10 certificate, a Certificate IV or diploma, a trade certificate, or relevant work experience. Graduate trainees need a bachelor degree from an Australian university. All applicants must obtain a security clearance and an Employment Suitability Clearance, and pass medical and fitness assessments .

faqs.q: How much do Australian Border Force recruits earn?
faqs.a: BFORT recruits earn at the APS3 classification, currently A$66,839 to A$76,792 per year, plus 15.4 per cent superannuation. Additional shift penalties and allowances apply during operational placements, and an enterprise agreement salary increase took effect in March 2026. After graduation, officers progress through the APS pay structure, with typical officer salaries reported around A$80,000 to A$90,000.

faqs.q: Where could you be posted after BFORT training?
faqs.a: After graduating you could work across Australia in diverse environments, from major cities to remote locations, including airports, seaports, detention and compliance operations, and regional posts. Officers must be willing to deploy at short notice and participate in active career management, which means postings change as operational needs evolve throughout your career.
